description: Risk-tier routing matrix. The router classifies a task by matching its intent/acceptance_criteria against these rules. The CORE PRINCIPLE: if the planner can write crisp, testable acceptance criteria up front, the work is offloadable; if defining 'done' needs judgment, it stays RED with the planner. The router may UPGRADE a manifest's declared tier (green->yellow->red) but never silently downgrades it.
principle: offloadable iff acceptance_criteria are deterministically checkable; otherwise red.

green.handling: Offload. Deterministic gate only. Auto-pass on exit-0. No LLM judge, no planner involvement.
examples: mechanical refactor or codemod with a verifiable transform
dependency version bump with passing build
search-and-summarize over the graph or a directory
green.requires: Every acceptance_criterion has a `verify` command, OR executor.mode == 'shell' with a deterministic eval_plan.

yellow.handling: Offload + LLM judge. Deterministic gate first; if it passes, the judge scores against acceptance_criteria. Below pass_threshold -> escalate per policy.
examples: feature implementation against a written spec
bug fix with a reproducing test
multi-file edit with a clear contract
data transform where output shape is specified but content needs judgment
yellow.requires: acceptance_criteria are clear but not all deterministically checkable; a repro or spec exists.

red.handling: Do NOT offload. Escalate to the planner (Claude). The orchestrator records the task and returns escalate=true without running the executor.
examples: cross-cutting changes touching the deterministic zone (L1/L2, manifests/, signing)
anything where acceptance criteria cannot be stated before doing the work
red.requires: Acceptance criteria require judgment to define, or the change touches a guarded surface.

force_red.description: If any of these match the intent or a touched path, the task is forced to red regardless of declared tier.

force_yellow.description: Green tasks carrying these signals are upgraded to yellow so a judge double-checks them.
force_yellow.no_verify_criteria: A declared-green task with any acceptance_criterion lacking a `verify` command is upgraded to yellow.

defaults._comment: Models confirmed serving on the operator's Lemonade (2026-06-29). qwen3.5-9b-FLM produces clean code and is the executor default. Judge = Phi-4-mini-instruct-NPU: in the head-to-head it reliably REJECTS bad code (safe failure mode), where the 0.5B sometimes rubber-stamped bad code 0.9 (false positive = dangerous). Phi is conservative (false-negatives some good code -> escalates), so YELLOW-task savings are modest; reliable savings come from GREEN shell/deterministic tasks. See JUDGE-CALIBRATION.md. GGUF/llamacpp recipes (Gemma-*) fail to load on this box.
